questions.subject: PHYSICS_I
questions.learningObjective: compute the distance fallen under gravity
questions.stem: An object is dropped from rest. How far does it fall in 2.0 seconds, in metres? Use g = 9.8 m/s^2. Report the number only.
questions.explanation: Distance from rest under constant acceleration is half g t squared, so half times 9.8 times 4 gives 19.6 metres. Using g t squared without the half would double the answer, and using g t would give the speed, not the distance.
questions.hint: Distance from rest is half g t squared.

questions.hint: Speed from rest is g times time.

questions.learningObjective: compute time to fall a given height
questions.stem: How long does it take an object dropped from rest to fall 20.0 metres? Use g = 9.8 m/s^2. Report seconds to two decimals.
questions.explanation: From h = half g t squared, t = sqrt(2h/g) = sqrt(40/9.8) = 2.02 s.
questions.hint: Solve h = half g t squared for t.
